text: Question: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 22-year-old client who is seeking treatment for constipation and given a prescription and discharge instructions for bisacodyl therapy. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
A. “I should drink 2 to 4 glasses of water per day.”
B. “I will take the medication on an empty stomach to obtain quick relief from constipation.”
C. “I will notify my health care provider if I should experience abdominal pain without any relief.”
D. “I should make sure that I do not take the medication with an antacid even to prevent gastric upset.”
E. “I should plan on taking the medication for the rest of my life to prevent any future episodes of discomfort.”
Correct answers: A. “I should drink 2 to 4 glasses of water per day.”; E. “I should plan on taking the medication for the rest of my life to prevent any future episodes of discomfort.”
notes: Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative for short-term use. Follow-up is needed for: drinking only 2–4 glasses of water (the client should take in about 8–10 glasses a day to help the laxative work and prevent dehydration) and planning to use it for life (long-term use causes dependence and electrolyte loss). Taking it on an empty stomach, reporting unrelieved abdominal pain, and avoiding antacids (they dissolve the enteric coating early) are all correct.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)
